simulatorVsEngine.verdict: identical on all 400 positions and orientations

parity.method: Common partition = the H-orbit partition. Every H-orbit is a union of G-orbits (verified), so G's generator parity vectors are re-expressed on H-orbits by XOR-ing the parities of the G-orbits inside each H-orbit; this was checked to equal the parity of the restriction to the H-orbit directly. Ranks on the native G-orbit partition are reported separately.

search.method: Bidirectional BFS on the state graph. The move group acts freely on the solved state, so an additional atom lies in G iff the state it produces is reachable with existing atoms only.

verdict.reason: 24 of 54 additional atoms have an orbit-parity vector outside the GF(2) span of G's generator parities (rank 5 of 11 orbits), which proves those atoms are not in G and hence that H is strictly larger and reaches states G cannot. The other 30 additional atoms break no invariant and were not expressed as words in G, so their own membership is undetermined.
